comment: These records distinguish literal source conditions from the author-approved corrections needed to state a coherent finite ordinal IID model. They do not claim the archive already entails the corrected clauses.

positive rate for each seller type.reason: The governing correction states 0 < g(theta) <= 1 for every type, which supplies the positivity premise used by asymptotic rate claims.
positive rate for each seller type.source_evidence: Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

premises: positive rate for each seller type
assumption_positive_match_rates.reason: Positive match rates are explicit in the author-approved corrected model so every seller's floor sample count diverges; the archive's nondecreasing-rate prose alone does not establish positivity.
assumption_positive_match_rates.source_evidence: Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

at most one floor-count increment per pe.reason: The source says at most one buyer matches per period; the exact floor-count step property is justified by the approved upper bound g(theta) <= 1.
at most one floor-count increment per pe.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:669-670 states at-most-one matching per period and a nondecreasing match function with floor accumulation. Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

monotone match rate.reason: The source explicitly assumes a nondecreasing match function by seller quality.
monotone match rate.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:669-670 states at-most-one matching per period and a nondecreasing match function with floor accumulation.

nonnegative match rate.reason: Positive corrected match rates imply nonnegative rates, but that strengthening is recorded as an author-approved correction rather than silently derived from prose.
nonnegative match rate.source_evidence: Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

premises: at most one floor-count increment per period
source_match_schedule_coherence.reason: The source explicitly gives a nondecreasing match function and at-most-one matching prose; the exact floor-step coherence and nonnegativity used by Lean are recorded through the author-approved 0 < g(theta) <= 1 correction.
source_match_schedule_coherence.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:669-670 states at-most-one matching per period and a nondecreasing match function with floor accumulation. Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

every displayed score is between zero an.reason: The source gives phi(y) in [0,1] for every rating y, which is the same two-sided bound.
every displayed score is between zero an.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:679-680 states that every rating score lies in [0,1].

premises: every displayed score is between zero and one
source_rating_scores_in_unit_interval.reason: The source explicitly restricts each rating score to the interval [0,1], matching the two-sided real inequality in the Lean predicate.
source_rating_scores_in_unit_interval.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:679-680 states that every rating score lies in [0,1].

strict decrease between adjacent display.reason: The finite adjacent-cutoff reading is the literal meaningful interpretation of strict decrease with the displayed ordinal rating level.
strict decrease between adjacent display.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:683 states that cumulative rating mass is strictly increasing in quality and strictly decreasing with rating level.

premises: strict decrease between adjacent displayed ordinal cutoffs
source_strict_ordinal_cumulative_tail_de.reason: The source says cumulative rating tails strictly decrease with rating level. Lean states that only between adjacent displayed cutoffs, avoiding an invented cutoff above the finite maximum.
source_strict_ordinal_cumulative_tail_de.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:683 states that cumulative rating mass is strictly increasing in quality and strictly decreasing with rating level. Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

strict cross-quality tail ordering above.reason: This is the author-approved repair of the archive's all-cutoff wording, preserving strict stochastic ordering wherever a nontrivial cutoff exists.
strict cross-quality tail ordering above.source_evidence: Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

premises: strict cross-quality tail ordering above the bottom cutoff
source_strict_ordinal_quality_tail_incre.reason: The archive says tails strictly increase with quality, but strictness at the bottom cutoff is impossible because that upper tail is always one. The approved correction restricts strictness to nonbottom displayed cutoffs.
source_strict_ordinal_quality_tail_incre.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:683 states that cumulative rating mass is strictly increasing in quality and strictly decreasing with rating level. Pinned docs/GOVERNING_CORRECTED_MODEL_2026-07-24.md:20-22 records the author-approved finite model clauses and their archival deltas.

strict monotonicity on the ordered ratin.reason: The source conditions its convergence claim on strict score increase, and the governing corrected model records strict increase as a model clause.
strict monotonicity on the ordered ratin.source_evidence: Pinned cited publication:744-745 explicitly conditions convergence prose on a strictly increasing score function. source_strictly_increasing_rating_scores.reason: Strict score monotonicity is invoked in the source convergence discussion and is made an explicit author-approved finite-ordinal model clause; it is not inferred from the weaker [0,1] range condition.
